QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_27

question.text: Asha Deep Trust claims 40% decrease in child-marriage rates in participating communities (Sakhi case). Under SAS-400, the MOST rigorous MoV is:

answer.text: A phone call to the Sarpanch
Triangulation of: (i) village marriage registers, (ii) school dropout data for girls aged 14-18, (iii) Panchayat records, (iv) sub-sample household visits

explanation.text: The Logic: Child-marriage rates are routinely under-reported, so single-source evidence is methodologically weak. Combining multiple independent sources — administrative marriage registers, girls' secondary-school retention data, local-body records, and sub-sample household visits — produces a defensible Means of Verification. This kind of multi-source triangulation, complemented by primary/secondary data, FGDs, observation, data-quality checks, and stakeholder validation, is the standard approach to corroborating an outcome claim. The Trap: Option A relies only on SE self-report. Option C is a single-informant source. Option B cites a national benchmark, which does not evidence project-attributable change. Note: The cited SIA workbook supports a 40% decrease in child-marriage rates for the Sakhi case and supports general primary/secondary-source, FGD, observation, data-quality and stakeholder-validation methods, but the specific village-register / school-dropout / Panchayat / household-visit triangulation phrasing is not stated. The framing above reflects general SIA evidence-gathering practice.
